meta.name: dasfax-ws4-calibration-v1
meta.purpose: Threshold calibration and CI regression guard for the Tier 2 screening models (WS4).
meta.provenance: SYNTHETIC. Every sample below was hand-authored for this repo. No sample is a real article, and no real person is quoted. Fake-labelled samples use invented specifics and are stylistic stand-ins for misinformation, not operational disinformation.
meta.honesty_note: This corpus is large enough to pick and defend an operating threshold, and small enough that its precision/recall figures must NOT be quoted to judges as model accuracy. The number to quote comes from a real held-out split (ISOT / Fakeddit): run `python ws4_eval.py --dataset path/to/isot.jsonl`.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Dengue cases fall for third straight week
text_samples.text: The National Environment Agency said dengue cases fell to 214 in the week ending 8 March, down from 287 the week before. According to the agency, 91 active clusters remain islandwide, with the largest in the eastern part of the country. A spokesperson said inspections of about 12,000 premises in February found mosquito breeding at 380 of them. Residents were advised to check flower pot plates and scupper drains weekly.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: HDB resale prices rise 1.2% in first quarter
text_samples.text: Resale flat prices rose 1.2 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, according to official figures released on Friday. That follows a 1.5 per cent increase in the previous quarter. Analysts at two local property consultancies said in a statement that supply from newly completed projects should moderate price growth over the rest of the year. A total of 6,842 resale transactions were recorded in the quarter, down 3 per cent year on year.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Train service resumes after signalling fault
text_samples.text: Train services on the affected stretch resumed at about 9.15am after a signalling fault caused delays of up to 25 minutes during the morning peak, the operator said. According to the operator, engineers traced the fault to a trackside component that was replaced overnight. Free bridging bus services were deployed between six stations for roughly 90 minutes. The transport regulator said it would review the incident report before deciding on any penalty.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Police report rise in impersonation scam cases
text_samples.text: Police said impersonation scam cases rose to 3,363 in 2025 from 1,504 in 2024. Total losses reported for the year reached S$242.9 million. In a statement, the police said victims were most commonly contacted through unsolicited calls and messaging applications. Officers advised members of the public to verify any request for payment through official channels before transferring money, and noted that government agencies do not ask for transfers over the phone.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Core inflation eases to 2.4% in February
text_samples.text: Core inflation eased to 2.4 per cent in February from 2.7 per cent in January, according to data from the statistics department. Services inflation was flat at 2.9 per cent, while food inflation moderated to 2.2 per cent. Economists at three banks said in research notes that the figure was broadly in line with expectations. The central bank has projected core inflation to average between 1.5 and 2.5 per cent for the full year.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: COE premiums close mixed in latest bidding
text_samples.text: Certificate of entitlement premiums closed mixed in the latest bidding exercise that ended on Wednesday. Premiums for smaller cars fell 2.1 per cent to S$96,300, while those for larger cars rose 0.8 per cent to S$118,001. The open category closed at S$117,500. Quota for the current three-month period stands at 4,832 certificates across all categories, according to figures published by the transport authority.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Study finds gap between confidence and accuracy in spotting false news
text_samples.text: A study by a local university found that while 79 per cent of respondents were confident they could identify false news, 91 per cent misidentified at least one of five test headlines. The researchers found that confidence was not correlated with accuracy in any age group surveyed. The study surveyed 1,200 respondents between June and August and was published in a peer-reviewed journal this month.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Port container throughput up 4.6% in 2025
text_samples.text: Container throughput at the port reached 41.2 million twenty-foot equivalent units in 2025, up 4.6 per cent from the previous year, according to data from the maritime authority. Bunker sales fell 1.3 per cent over the same period. The authority said in a statement that capacity at the new terminal berths would be expanded in phases through 2027.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: New bus service to link two towns from April
text_samples.text: A new bus service linking two housing estates will begin operating on 6 April, the transport authority announced on Tuesday. The service will run at intervals of 12 to 18 minutes during peak hours and will call at 21 stops along its route. According to the authority, the service was introduced after a public consultation exercise in which about 4,000 residents took part.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Employment rises for fourth consecutive quarter
text_samples.text: Total employment rose by 8,400 in the fourth quarter, marking a fourth consecutive quarterly increase, according to preliminary labour market figures. The overall unemployment rate held steady at 2.0 per cent. The manpower ministry said in a statement that growth was concentrated in the information and communications and financial services sectors, while retrenchments fell to 2,910 from 3,240 in the preceding quarter.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Central bank holds benchmark rate steady
text_samples.text: The central bank held its benchmark interest rate steady at 4.25 per cent on Thursday, in a decision that matched the expectations of most economists surveyed before the meeting. In a statement, the bank said inflation had continued to moderate but remained above its 2 per cent target. Two of the nine committee members voted for a quarter-point reduction. The next policy meeting is scheduled for June.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Magnitude 6.1 earthquake reported offshore
text_samples.text: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck about 120km offshore at a depth of 35km on Sunday morning, according to the national seismological agency. No tsunami warning was issued. Local authorities said in a statement that there were no immediate reports of casualties, and that inspections of bridges and older buildings in the two nearest districts were under way.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Company reports 12% rise in quarterly revenue
text_samples.text: The company reported revenue of 4.8 billion for the quarter, up 12 per cent from a year earlier, according to results published on Monday. Operating margin narrowed to 18.2 per cent from 19.6 per cent, which the company attributed to higher component costs. The chief financial officer said in a statement that full-year guidance was unchanged. Shares closed 2.4 per cent lower following the announcement.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Court upholds ruling in data protection case
text_samples.text: An appeals court upheld a lower court ruling in a data protection case on Wednesday, according to court documents released the same day. The three-judge panel found that the regulator had acted within its statutory powers when it issued the original penalty. The company said in a statement it was reviewing the judgment. The penalty, first issued in 2024, was set at 1.1 million.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Study links urban tree cover to lower daytime temperatures
text_samples.text: Researchers found that neighbourhoods with tree canopy cover above 30 per cent recorded daytime surface temperatures an average of 1.8 degrees Celsius lower than comparable areas below 10 per cent cover. The study analysed satellite imagery from 46 cities collected between 2019 and 2024. According to the authors, the effect was strongest in the late afternoon. The paper was published in a peer-reviewed journal on Monday.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Airline adds three routes for winter schedule
text_samples.text: The airline will add three routes to its winter schedule from 28 October, according to a filing published this week. Two of the routes will be served four times weekly and the third daily. A spokesperson said the additions reflect a 9 per cent increase in planned seat capacity compared with the same period last year. Ticket sales opened on Friday.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Water demand projected to rise by 2065
text_samples.text: The national water agency projects that total water demand could nearly double by 2065, with the non-domestic sector accounting for about 70 per cent of the total. According to the agency, desalination and reclaimed water are expected to meet up to 85 per cent of demand by then. Household consumption averaged 141 litres per person per day in 2025, down from 143 litres the year before.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Primary school registration exercise opens
text_samples.text: Registration for the annual primary school admission exercise opened on Tuesday and will run in phases until September, the education ministry said. According to the ministry, 33 schools were oversubscribed at the equivalent stage last year and required balloting. Parents were advised to check vacancy figures published daily on the ministry website before submitting an application.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Regulator fines telecom operator over outage
text_samples.text: The telecommunications regulator fined an operator 3.2 million over a nationwide outage that lasted about seven hours in November, according to a statement published on Thursday. The regulator found that the operator had not maintained adequate redundancy at two core network sites. The operator said in a statement that it had since completed remedial work and would not appeal the decision.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Vaccination coverage reaches 89% among older adults
text_samples.text: Influenza vaccination coverage among adults aged 65 and above reached 89 per cent this season, up from 84 per cent last season, according to health authority figures. The authority said in a statement that mobile vaccination teams visited 210 residential sites between October and January. Coverage among adults aged 18 to 49 remained lower, at 41 per cent.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Public consultation opens on cycling path rules
text_samples.text: A six-week public consultation on proposed changes to cycling path rules opened on Monday, according to the transport authority. The proposals include a lower speed limit on shared paths and clearer signage at 340 junctions. The authority said feedback received during a previous exercise in 2024, which drew about 7,600 responses, informed the current draft. Submissions close on 15 May.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.title: Retail sales edge up 0.6% in January
text_samples.text: Retail sales rose 0.6 per cent year on year in January, according to figures published by the statistics department on Friday. Excluding motor vehicles, sales were up 1.1 per cent. Department store sales fell 2.3 per cent, while online sales accounted for 13.8 per cent of the retail total. Economists noted that the timing of the festive period made month-on-month comparisons less meaningful.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.note: HARD NEGATIVE — legitimate court reporting leans on 'allegedly' constantly
text_samples.title: Three charged over alleged investment scheme
text_samples.text: Three men were charged on Tuesday over an alleged investment scheme that police say took in about 2.4 million from 61 investors. The men allegedly told investors the funds would be placed in overseas property. According to charge sheets, the scheme allegedly ran from March 2024 to January 2026. All three allegedly continued accepting deposits after the regulator issued a warning. The case was adjourned to 14 April.

text_samples.label: real
text_samples.note: HARD NEGATIVE — genuine investigative journalism uses 'documents show', 'cover-up'
text_samples.title: Internal documents show regulator was warned two years before collapse
text_samples.text: Internal documents obtained under freedom of information laws show the regulator received detailed warnings about the firm 26 months before it collapsed. According to the documents, three separate assessments flagged the same liquidity risk. A former official said in an interview that concerns were escalated but not acted upon. The regulator said in a statement it accepted the findings and had since changed its escalation process. Critics have described the delay as a cover-up.

text_samples.title: MOH, HDB and CPF changes take effect from April
text_samples.text: MOH said the revised subsidy tiers take effect on 1 April, according to a joint statement with MOF. HDB confirmed that CPF housing grant limits will be adjusted at the same time. LTA said COE quota changes announced earlier remain unchanged, while IRAS confirmed the GST treatment is unaffected. MOM, IMDA and CSA were also consulted during the review, which began in 2025.

text_samples.title: Police advisory: new variant of impersonation scam
text_samples.text: Police issued an advisory on Monday about a new variant of the government official impersonation scam. According to the advisory, victims received calls from someone claiming to be an officer and were told their bank accounts were involved in money laundering. Police said no government agency will ask for bank transfers over the phone. Members of the public are urged to share this advisory with elderly relatives and to verify any such call through official hotlines.

According to the agency, the affected batch code is printed on the base of the tin. Consumers who bought the product were told to stop using it immediately and return it for a full refund. The importer said in a statement that the batch had been withdrawn from all retailers.
